 Judgment
The appellants are the petitioners in O.P(MV) No.901/2006 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mavelikara.
They have preferred an application under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the M.V.Act') claiming compensation of 7,00,000/- for death of the victim.
2. According to the appellants, on 10.3.2006, at about 12 pm, on the Avoor-Muttom public road, the victim was riding a scooter from south to north direction.

When he reached the spot of the accident,
an autorickshaw was driven at high speed against him.

In order to avoid the accident, the scooter was suddenly turned left, thereby losing control over the scooter and it went into the neighbouring property and hit a tree, causing the victim fatal injuries and he succumbed to death on the way to the Government Hospital, Kayamkulam.
3. The first respondent is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle and he holds a valid insurance policy with the second respondent.
The tribunal dismissed the claim petition, which was filed under Section 163A of the M.V.Act, stating that since the yearly income claimed exceeds 40,000/-, the petition is not maintainable.
Challenging the same, the claimants have come up in appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and the 2024:KER:73779 MACA NO. 1953 OF 2014 learned standing counsel appearing for the second respondent.

5. The Learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants submits that due to inadvertent omission, the compensation for the death of the victim was valued at 7,00,000/- and the income claimed for the deceased was 7000/- per month and thus the yearly income exceeded 40,000/-.
It is also submitted that though the appellants intended to file an amendment petition, the same was omitted to be done.
Since no amendment petition was filed, the tribunal had dismissed the original petition as not maintainable.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that when the impugned Aliyamma George vs P. Georgekutty on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138491307/
2 order was passed by the tribunal on 20/1/2014, neither the appellants nor their counsel was present.
However, the order passed by the tribunal does not reflect any such endorsement.

6. Learned Standing Counsel for the second respondent- the New India Assurance Company submits that under Section 163A of the M.V.Act, the annual income should not have exceeded 40,000/-, but the appellants claimed the income of the deceased as 7000/- per month, which is not permissible under law and hence the order of the tribunal does not need any interference.

7. Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the tribunal ought to have considered the question as to whether the claim is maintainable 2024:KER:73779 MACA NO. 1953 OF 2014 under Section 166 of the M.V.Act before dismissing the claim petition.
8. The order passed by the tribunal is cryptic.

The tribunal has not stated whether the petitioner/appellant was given an opportunity to adduce evidence or an opportunity for the petitioner to amend the claim petition to convert it into a petition under Section 166 or to amend the income shown.
The claim petition is put forth by the legal heirs of the deceased, who was the sole bread winner of the family.

Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the award dated 20/01/20214 in O.P(MV) No.901/2006 of the M.A.C.T., Mavelikara is to be set aside and the appellant/claimant has to be given one more opportunity to contest the case in whichever manner,
in accordance with law.
9.

Accordingly, the award dated 20/01/2014 in O.P(MV) No.901/2006 of the M.A.C.T.
(Addl.District & Sessions Judge-II), Mavelikara is set aside and the matter is remanded back to the tribunal for fresh consideration.
Parties are directed to appear before the tribunal on 30/10/2024.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

Sd/-
SHOBA ANNAMMA EAPEN, JUDGE MBS/
